title: Keys and Rooms
statement:
A building has `n` rooms numbered `0` to `n - 1`. Room `0` is open; every other room stays locked until you hold its key. `rooms[i]` lists the keys lying in room `i`: key `k` opens room `k`, and once you enter a room you keep all its keys and can use them any number of times.

Starting in room `0`, return `true` if you can eventually enter every room, and `false` otherwise.
constraints: The keys inside each room are distinct
notes:
## Intuition

Treat each room as a node and each key `k` found in room `i` as a directed edge `i -> k`. Keys are never used up, so the rooms you can enter are exactly the nodes reachable from room `0`. One depth-first search from room `0` marks them all; the answer is whether it reached all `n`. (A slower idea repeatedly sweeps every opened room and collects keys until nothing changes, which can take O(n) sweeps.)

## Approach

1. Make a `visited` array, mark room `0`, push it on a `stack`, and set `count = 1`.
2. While the stack is not empty, pop a `room`.
3. For each `key` in that room, if its room is not yet `visited`, mark it, increase `count` and push it.
4. Return whether `count` equals the number of rooms.

## Example 1, step by step

`rooms = [[1],[2],[3],[]]`. Start with `stack = [0]`, `count = 1`. Pop room 0: key 1 is new, so `count = 2`, `stack = [1]`. Pop room 1: key 2 is new, `count = 3`. Pop room 2: key 3 is new, `count = 4`. Pop room 3: no keys. The stack is empty and `count = 4 = rooms.length`, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + k), where k is the total number of keys: each room is pushed once and each key is read once.
- Space: O(n) for `visited` and the stack.

## Pitfalls

- Mark a room as visited when you push it, not when you pop it, or the same room can be pushed many times.
- Room `0` starts open even if no key for it exists; count it from the start.
- A room may hold its own key or keys to rooms already open; those must not change `count`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `visited` | `visited[r]` is true once room `r` has been reached |
| `stack` | rooms reached whose keys are still to be collected |
| `count` | how many distinct rooms have been reached |
| `room` | the room whose keys are being read |
| `key` | one key in that room, i.e. the room it opens |

narration.2: No room has been reached yet, so every flag starts false.
narration.3: The search starts from room 0, the only open room.
narration.4: Mark room 0 as reached right away.
narration.5: count tracks how many rooms have been reached; room 0 is the first.
narration.7: Keep going while some reached room still has keys to collect.
narration.8: Take the most recently reached room off the stack.
narration.9: Look at every key lying in that room.
narration.10: Only a room we have not reached before matters.
narration.11: Mark it when it is pushed so it is never pushed twice.
narration.12: One more room can be entered.
narration.13: Its keys still need to be collected, so push it.
narration.17: Every room is reachable exactly when the search reached all of them.
